chunks: Abu al-Abbas ibn 'Uqdah from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Hazim, who said: Taghlib ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, who said: Bishr ibn Ja'far al-Ju'fi, Abu al-Walid, said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying:
"The House (Kaaba) is the qiblah for the people of the mosque, and the mosque is the qiblah for the people of the Haram, and the Haram is the qiblah for all people."

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْحَرَمِ: The people of the Haram (those in the broader sanctuary of Mecca)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمَسْجِدِ: The people of the mosque (residents of Mecca)
key_terms.الْحَرَمُ: The Haram (the sacred sanctuary of Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct direction of prayer for Muslims living outside Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the jurisprudential principle of *Tawassul* in direction, establishing a concentric hierarchy where the Kaaba is the focal point for those within the Masjid al-Haram, the broader Haram for those in Mecca, and the entire region for the global Ummah. This structure reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of spatial flexibility in prayer, ensuring that the sanctity of the Kaaba remains the central axis of worship regardless of the believer's location. It underscores the theological concept that the Kaaba is not merely a physical object but a spiritual center radiating outward to encompass the entire world.
